summary.format: 108/108 (light check over all runs: all five labels present in every final report)

five_labels_named_in_harness_prompt.note: every one of the 108 final reports carries Done:/Failed:, Steps:, Check:, Look: and Notes:. Iteration 9 scored 65/108 on format; naming the labels in the harness prompt closed the gap completely.

failed_label_on_a_successful_information.note: rep1/j07-probe wrote 'Failed: 編集の実行は依頼されていないため何も書き出していません' for a comparison that fully succeeded. All three e10-highlights runs and the other two j07 runs correctly used Done: for an analysis-only job.

language_drift.note: all 24 Japanese requests (j01-j08 x3) plus r02-tts, f02-corrupt-input and x03-audio-trim were answered in Japanese. The three drifts are all English requests: r04-translate drifts into the language the request talks about, x05 and e02 drift with no prompt trigger at all.

font_by_script_1_11_fix.note: the first lower-third render used the default font and produced tofu for 「山田 太郎 / プロデューサー」. The agent spotted it on a look.py frame, re-ran with --font-file /usr/share/fonts/opentype/ipafont-gothic/ipag.ttf and verified. Self-recovered, but it cost an extra render - exactly what the 1.11 font-by-script default is meant to remove.

render_py_stray_srt.note: render.py wrote 'cues.srt (3 cues)' with no directory prefix, i.e. next to the caption source rather than into final_work/. In this run the agent had already copied cues.txt into OUTDIR, so the stray landed in OUTDIR (harmless here). Had it pointed render.py at /home/user/ffmpeg-skill/tests/out/cues.txt directly, the .srt would have been written into the repo's test fixtures. rep1 and rep2 j08 produced no cues.srt.

agents_reading_evals_json.note: grep for 'ffmpeg-skill/evals' and 'agent_prompts' across all 108 run.md files returns nothing. The iteration-9 behaviour (rep2/r04-translate quoting the prompt file) did not recur.

findings: Format is now perfect: 108/108 reports carry all five labels, up from 65/108 in iteration 9. Naming the labels in the harness prompt was decisive.

Three language drifts remain (rep1/x05-replace-audio es, rep3/e02-cut-lossless pt, rep3/r04-translate es). Two have no prompt trigger at all, so this is model noise rather than a rule the skill fails to state.

All 30 refusal/failure runs are honest: every one names what was refused or what failed, quotes the tool's own error where there was one, and writes no output. No fabricated result anywhere in the graded set.

The recurring soft spot is the Look: line. On audio-only jobs agents variously put the output path, listening advice, or 'not needed' there (rep2/e08, rep3/e08, rep2/x02, rep1/e02); on rep1/e09-join a picture-changing edit shipped with no contact sheet at all.

rep1/j07-probe is the only 'Failed:' misuse: a successful comparison reported as a failure because nothing was written. The label choice should hinge on whether the job succeeded, not on whether a file was produced.
rep3/j03-lower shows the font problem the 1.11 fix targets: default font -> tofu -> self-caught -> re-render. Correct final result, one wasted encode.
rep2/f05-unsupported contradicts itself in Notes: ('denoise.py can add grain-like noise') after correctly saying denoise removes grain.
harness_or_model_issues: The three language drifts are model-side; none of the three prompts contains a non-English word except r04's target language.
render.py's relative cues.srt path (rep3/j08-project) is a skill bug, not a harness one: with an un-copied caption source it writes into the repo fixture directory.
No agent read the eval definitions under /home/user/ffmpeg-skill/evals this iteration.
scenes.py --highlights 2 can only return one range on the 12 s single-scene fixture; all three e10 runs handled it honestly, but the fixture cannot exercise the multi-highlight path.
